newsitem.title: JAPAN: Coastguard says Tokyo tanker spill Japan's worst.
newsitem.headline: Coastguard says Tokyo tanker spill Japan's worst.

text.p: Japan's coastguard said an estimated 13,400 tonnes of crude oil leaked from a supertanker which struck a reef in Tokyo Bay on Wednesday, making it Japan's worst ever oil spill.

Wednesday's oil slick from the 259,999 deadweight-tonne Panamanian-flagged Diamond Grace spread to an area about 5.5 km (3.4 miles) long and 4.5 km (2.8 miles) wide in the middle of Tokyo Bay, said a spokesman for the regional headquarters of the Maritime Safety Agency, or coastguard, in Yokohama.

In January, 5,200 tonnes of heavy fuel oil leaked from a Russian tanker which capsized in the stormy Sea of Japan, until then Japan's worst oil tanker spill. The tanker had been carrying 19,000 tonnes of fuel oil when it went down.

The Diamond Grace scraped a shallow reef on Wednesday morning, rupturing at least two of its crude oil tanks, coastguard and shipping company officials said. The tanker's operator, Nippon Yusen KK, said the two tanks held 38,600 tonnes of crude.
The ship, a very large crude carrier (VLCC), was carrying a total of 257,000 tonnes of crude oil from the United Arab Emirates to a refinery in Kawasaki, south of Tokyo.
